questions.stem: Q1. A 65 y/o male with coronary artery disease (CAD) is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient is stable on medications with no recent chest pain or dyspnea. The anesthesiologist selects anaesthetic agents for the patient. Which of the following options is false regarding the choice of agents?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A 65 y/o male with coronary artery disease (CAD) is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient is stable on medications with no recent chest pain or dyspnea. The anesthesiologist selects anaesthetic agents for the patient. Which of the following options is false regarding the choice of agents?

options.label: A
options.text: Propofol is used in CAD patients as the intravenous anaesthetic agent of choice.

options.label: B
options.text: Isoflurane is used as an inhalational agent for patients with good myocardial contractility.

options.label: C
options.text: Vecuronium is used as a muscle relaxant for cardiac patients.

options.label: D
options.text: Etomidate is used as an intravenous anaesthetic agent.

questions.stem: Q1. Which of the following is true about brain death?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. Which of the following is true about brain death?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete loss of cerebral cortical function but preservation of brainstem reflexes.

options.label: B
options.text: Irreversible loss of all brain function, including the brainstem, with inability to breathe independently.

options.label: C
options.text: Persistent vegetative state where higher brain functions are lost, but spontaneous respiratory effort is present.

options.label: D
options.text: Reversible coma with absence of brainstem reflexes.

questions.stem: Q1. A male patient presents for an elective total knee replacement. During the preoperative assessment, the anesthesiologist performs a thorough evaluation and finds: Mallampati Score: Class III Thyromental Distance: 6 cm Sterno-mental distance 13 cm with head in maximum extension Neck circumference of 16 inch Which of the following features in a patient would prompt you to anticipate a difficult intubation?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A male patient presents for an elective total knee replacement. During the preoperative assessment, the anesthesiologist performs a thorough evaluation and finds: Mallampati Score: Class III Thyromental Distance: 6 cm Sterno-mental distance 13 cm with head in maximum extension Neck circumference of 16 inch Which of the following features in a patient would prompt you to anticipate a difficult intubation?

options.label: C
options.text: Sterno-mental distance 13cm with head in maximum extension

questions.stem: Q1. A 45-year-old woman is undergoing elective cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist is using halothane as the primary inhalational anesthetic. During the procedure, the surgeon encounters unexpected bleeding and requests local infiltration with adrenaline (epinephrine) for hemostasis. What is the most appropriate response of the anesthesiologist to the surgeon's request for adrenaline infiltration?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A 45-year-old woman is undergoing elective cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist is using halothane as the primary inhalational anesthetic. During the procedure, the surgeon encounters unexpected bleeding and requests local infiltration with adrenaline (epinephrine) for hemostasis. What is the most appropriate response of the anesthesiologist to the surgeon's request for adrenaline infiltration?

options.label: A
options.text: Agree to the use of adrenaline without any concerns

options.label: B
options.text: Refuse the use of adrenaline completely due to high-risk

options.label: C
options.text: Allow the use of adrenaline, but advise using a dilute solution and limiting the total dose

options.label: D
options.text: Suggest switching to a different inhalational anesthetic before using adrenaline

questions.stem: Q1. Which of the following is true regarding the history and development of anesthesia?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. Which of the following is true regarding the history and development of anesthesia?

options.label: A
options.text: Ether was introduced by Dr. Joseph O'Dwyer in 1842.

options.label: B
options.text: Chloroform was first used by Dr. Crawford Long in 1847.

options.label: C
options.text: William Morton demonstrated the use of ether as a general anesthetic in 1846.

options.label: D
options.text: Propofol was first introduced as an anesthetic in 1932.

questions.stem: Q1. A patient undergoing rapid sequence induction of anaesthesia receives succinylcholine as a muscle relaxant. Shortly after administration, the anesthesiologist notices muscle fasciculations followed by flaccid paralysis. What is the mechanism responsible for these observed effects?
questions.stemHtml: Q1. A patient undergoing rapid sequence induction of anaesthesia receives succinylcholine as a muscle relaxant. Shortly after administration, the anesthesiologist notices muscle fasciculations followed by flaccid paralysis. What is the mechanism responsible for these observed effects?

options.label: A
options.text: Prolonged depolarization of the muscle membrane

options.label: B
options.text: Competitive inhibition of Ach at the neuromuscular junction
